open_points.subject: ProjectViewerGrant revocation followed by re-grant
open_points.text:
A revoked grant is terminal and no operation reactivates it; giving the pair access again creates a new grant record.

INV-005: a revoked grant, credential, viewer, or session blocks the next authorization check immediately, per the revocation cascade table
open_points.question: If an administrator revokes a viewer grant and creates a new active grant before the viewer's next authorization check, must that check admit the viewer through the new grant or still fail because a revoked grant exists?
options: The new active grant restores access; the blocking guarantee lasts only while no replacement active grant exists.
The first check after every revocation must fail even if a replacement grant has already been created.
Re-granting is delayed or refused until a post-revocation authorization check has failed.
open_points.default_guess: The new active grant restores access; rewrite INV-005 so a revoked grant blocks authorization only in the absence of a later active grant for the pair.

witness.initial: A viewer has active grant G1 for project P.
events: Before the viewer makes another request, an administrator grants the same viewer access to P again, creating active grant G2.
The viewer makes a project-scoped read request for P.
outcomes: The request succeeds because G2 is active.
The request is refused because G1's revocation must block the next authorization check.

open_points.subject: StaffProjectAssignment revocation followed by reassignment
open_points.text:
A revoked assignment is terminal and no operation reactivates it; assigning the pair again creates a new assignment record.

INV-017: an operator may access a project only through one active StaffProjectAssignment; revocation blocks the next project-scoped authorization check immediately; current administrators derive project scope from the single administrative area policy
open_points.question: If an operator is reassigned before the first authorization check after revocation, does the new active assignment admit that check or does INV-017 require it to fail?
options: The new active assignment admits the operator; revocation blocks checks only while no replacement active assignment exists.
The first check after revocation fails even after reassignment.
Reassignment cannot take effect until a post-revocation check has failed.
open_points.default_guess: The new active assignment admits the operator; qualify INV-017 by the absence of a later active assignment.

witness.initial: Operator S has active assignment A1 for project P.
events: The administrator assigns S to P again, creating active assignment A2.
S performs the next project-scoped authorization check for P.
outcomes: The check fails because revocation of A1 must block the next check immediately.

open_points.subject: ProducerProjectGrant revocation followed by re-grant
open_points.text:
A revoked grant is terminal and no operation reactivates it; granting the pair again creates a new grant record.

INV-005: a revoked grant, credential, viewer, or session blocks the next authorization check immediately, per the revocation cascade table
open_points.question: For a granted_projects producer re-granted before its next import, does the replacement active grant authorize that import or must the old revocation still block it?
options: The replacement active grant authorizes the import.
The first import after revocation is refused even though a replacement grant is active.
A replacement producer grant cannot take effect until an authorization check has failed.
open_points.default_guess: The replacement active grant authorizes the import; qualify INV-005 accordingly.

witness.initial: A granted_projects producer has active grant G1 for project P.
events: The administrator creates replacement active grant G2 for the same producer and project.
The producer submits an import for P.
outcomes: The import passes the scope step because G2 is active.
The import is refused because G1's revocation must block the next authorization check.

open_points.subject: ProjectViewerGrant, StaffProjectAssignment and ProducerProjectGrant active-row uniqueness
open_points.kind: missing formal invariant and required test
open_points.text:
at most one active grant per `(viewer_id, project_id)`

at most one active assignment per `(staff_id, project_id)`

at most one active grant per `(principal, project)`
open_points.question: Which State 2 formal invariant and Required tests item must establish that each pair can have at most one active record, including when two creations contend?
options: Define one shared access-record invariant covering all three record types and require tests to show that no admissible history commits two active rows for a pair.
Define a separate invariant and Required tests item for each record type.
Do not make this a formal invariant, leaving the partial unique index as the only statement.
open_points.default_guess: Define one shared invariant with explicit Required tests showing that each pair has zero or one active row after sequential and contending creation attempts; leave the enforcement mechanism to its later owner.

witness.initial: No active viewer grant exists for viewer V and project P.
events: Two administrator operations both attempt to grant V access to P before either observes the other's result.
outcomes: Exactly one operation commits and exactly one active grant exists.
Both operations commit and two active grants exist because State 2 supplied no invariant or required proof for the changed rule.
witness.observer: The administrator and subsequent authorization checks

open_points.subject: Renewed access-record lifecycle and retained history
open_points.kind: missing formal invariant and required test
open_points.text:
A revoked grant is terminal and no operation reactivates it; giving the pair access again creates a new grant record.

A revoked assignment is terminal and no operation reactivates it; assigning the pair again creates a new assignment record.

A revoked grant is terminal and no operation reactivates it; granting the pair again creates a new grant record.
open_points.question: What formal invariant and Required tests item must show that re-granting or reassignment creates a distinct identity, leaves every old record revoked and unchanged, and never reactivates or replaces a historical row?
options: A shared immutable-history invariant covers the three record types and requires distinct IDs and unchanged old rows.
Three record-specific invariants cover those guarantees.
Only the resulting active access matters; preservation and identity of the revoked rows are not guaranteed.
open_points.default_guess: Use a shared immutable-history invariant with tests showing distinct new IDs, unchanged revoked rows, and no reactivation.

open_points.subject: Access-record revocation metadata
open_points.kind: missing formal invariant and required test
open_points.text: `revoked_at` and `revoked_by` are both null while the record is active and are both set, once, when it becomes revoked.
open_points.question: What formal invariant and Required tests item must show the null coupling, atomic transition, actor provenance and write-once behavior of revoked_at and revoked_by for all three changed record types?
options: Define one shared revocation-metadata invariant and test it for viewer grants, staff assignments and producer grants.
Define one invariant per record type.
Treat the field rule as sufficient without a Required tests item.
open_points.default_guess: Define one shared revocation-metadata invariant and require tests showing both fields change together exactly once and remain unchanged thereafter.

witness.initial: An active grant has revoked_at = None and revoked_by = None.
events: A later operation encounters the already revoked record.
outcomes: Both fields are set atomically on the first revocation and the later operation cannot alter either value.
One field is left null or a later operation overwrites the original time or actor because no State 2 invariant and required proof covers the rule.
witness.observer: An administrator inspecting persisted history or an audit investigation

open_points.subject: Visibility of revoked access records
open_points.kind: missing required result and invariant test
open_points.text: No product operation lists revoked records: a read by pair returns the active record only, and the history serves the audit trail.
open_points.question: Must State 2 guarantee that every product-facing lookup and list excludes revoked records, what result is returned when only history exists, and what Required tests demonstrate that the retained history cannot leak through product operations?
options: All product-facing reads exclude revoked records; a pair lookup with no active row returns the same absence result as a pair with no history.
Pair lookup excludes history, but administrator lists may include revoked rows.
Retained rows may be returned by unspecified product reads even though no operation is described as listing them.
open_points.default_guess: All product-facing reads exclude revoked rows and a pair with only revoked history is indistinguishable from a pair with no active record; add a shared invariant and Required tests for all three record types.

witness.initial: Viewer V has revoked grant G1 for project P and no active replacement.
events: An administrator performs the product's pair lookup for V and P.
The administrator performs every available product list involving viewer grants.
outcomes: The pair lookup reports no active grant and no list reveals G1.
A lookup or list returns G1 because the text does not state the required absence result or bind the rule to a test.

open_points.subject: Creation of an already-active grant or assignment
open_points.text:
since the grant operation refuses an active duplicate itself, State 4

since the operation refuses an active duplicate itself, State 4
open_points.question: What required refusal result applies when an administrator creates a viewer grant, staff assignment or producer grant for a pair that already has an active record, and must the attempt leave the existing row and every other table unchanged?
options: A typed conflict refusal with no state change and no audit record.
An idempotent success returning or identifying the existing active record.
A concealed or validation refusal with no state change.
A persistence failure exposed as an internal error.
open_points.default_guess: A typed conflict refusal with every table unchanged and no audit record, because A13 says these refused operations otherwise roll back and write no record.

witness.initial: Pair X/P already has active access record G1.
events: An administrator submits the corresponding grant or assignment operation again.
outcomes: The operation returns a defined conflict refusal and changes nothing.
The operation returns success, a validation error or an internal persistence error depending on the later implementation.

open_points.subject: Timestamps on renewable grants and assignments
open_points.text:
`created_at: datetime`

`revoked_at: datetime | None`

`revoked_at` and `revoked_by` are both null while the record is active and are both set, once, when it becomes revoked.
open_points.question: What is the authoritative source and representation of created_at and revoked_at, how many time readings does each create or revoke operation take, and must the same operation instant also be used for its AuditRecord.occurred_at?
options: UTC timezone-aware datetime from one injected authority reading per operation, shared by the access record and its audit record.
UTC datetime from separate authority readings for the access record and audit record.
Naive UTC datetime from one or more readings.
Storage-generated timestamps whose precision and relation to audit time are unspecified.
open_points.default_guess: Use a UTC timezone-aware datetime from one authoritative reading per mutating operation and share that instant with all timestamps written by that operation, including the audit record.

witness.initial: An administrator is about to revoke an active grant.
events: The revocation operation obtains or generates time.
It writes revoked_at and the required audit record's occurred_at.
outcomes: Both fields contain one identical, timezone-aware UTC instant.
They differ, are naive, or come from different clocks because State 2 did not decide source, representation or reading count.
witness.observer: An audit investigator comparing the grant history with AuditRecord

open_points.subject: Revoke access operation contracts with historical rows
open_points.text:
revoked grants of the pair stay as history

revoked assignments of the pair stay as history

No product operation lists revoked records: a read by pair returns the active record only
open_points.question: What must callers supply to identify the record being revoked now that a pair can have several historical records, and what failure may callers rely on when the pair has no active record?
options: The caller supplies the pair; the operation resolves and revokes its sole active record and returns a defined no-active-record failure otherwise.
The caller supplies the active record's grant_id or assignment_id; stale or revoked IDs return a defined failure.
The caller supplies both pair and record ID, and a mismatch is refused.
consequences: Pair-based contracts hide historical identities but require an exact no-active-row result.
ID-based contracts make the intended record explicit but expose record identity to callers and require stale-ID semantics.
Supplying both detects stale clients and cross-pair mistakes but enlarges every contract.
open_points.requirement:
A revoked grant is terminal and no operation reactivates it; giving the pair access again creates a new grant record.
A revoked assignment is terminal and no operation reactivates it; assigning the pair again creates a new assignment record.
A revoked grant is terminal and no operation reactivates it; granting the pair again creates a new grant record.
open_points.default_guess: State 5 should use the pair, resolve only the active row and define a no-active-record failure; it must preserve the quoted terminal-history and new-record guarantees.
